 -5-  MFA No. 9622 of 2018  C/W MFA No. 5593 of 2018  MFA No. 5594 of 2018  MFA No. 9623 of 2018  JUDGMENT 1.
The owner of the offending vehicle and claimants are in appeal.

Sri. Chimnaram vs Sri. Nanjappa on 20 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/121292577/
4 2.
The owner of the vehicle contends that exoneration of liability on the insurer is incorrect, since the vehicle is insured.
3. The claimants contend that the sum awarded by the Tribunal is meagre and requires to be enhanced.
4. The Tribunal had exonerated the Insurer on the ground that the policy particulars were not furnished.
5. During the pendency of these appeals, the claimants have produced the policy particulars and it is admitted by the insurer that the vehicle in question was insured.

In this view of the matter, the exoneration of liability on the insurer will have to be set aside and have to be held that the insurer is liable to satisfy the compensation amount awarded by the Tribunal.

6. As far as compensation is concerned, in all these cases, the Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.25,000/- towards 'pain and sufferings' and Rs.10,000/- towards 'conveyance, attendant charges,
food and nourishment.

7. In my view, the compensation is enhanced to a total sum of Rs.50,000/- to each of the claimants as against the sum of Rs.35,000/- each awarded by the Tribunal and the interest at the rate of 8%
per annum is required to be reduced to 6% per annum.
8.
The appeals filed by claimants are accordingly allowed in part.
The appeals filed by owner of the offending vehicle are allowed.

9. The claimants are entitled to a sum of Rs.50,000/- each along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realisation and the insurer is held liable to pay the enhanced compensation along with interest.
10. The amount in deposit, if any, shall be refunded to the owner of the offending vehicle.
